newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk debt tighter after news.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk debt tighter after news.

text.p: Bonds of Niagara Mohawk Power Corp tightened by at least 10 basis points across the board following news that a contract restructuring agreement was reached, traders said.
"This agreement definitely puts a positive spin on things," said one utilities trader. "Niagara Mohawk bonds have tightened at least 10 basis points, in some cases better than that."
Niagara Mohawk's 6-5/8 percent paper due 2005 were quoted 10 basis points tighter at 128 bid. Its 8.0 percent bonds due 2004 were 14 basis points tighter at 128 bid, traders said.

Niagara Mohawk and 16 Independent Power Producers (IPP) said on Thursday they had signed a master restructuring agreement to terminate or restructure 29 IPP contracts representing more than 80 percent of Niagara's above-market IPP costs.
In exchange for terminating or restructuring these contracts, the IPPs will receive approximately $3.6 billion in cash and 46 million shares of Niagara Stock.
The transaction was expected to reduce electricity prices for Niagara customers and to help expedite competition.

William Davis, chairman and chief executive officer of Niagara, said in a statement, "We are replacing a large and growing financial commitment with a defined debt obligation. The improved cash flow we expect to realize should allow us to begin immediately to reduce that debt.
"We seek to rebuild shareholder value, reduce prices for our customers and implement our plans to create a competitive power market for New York electricity consumers," he added.
Following news of the restructuring agreement, credit rating agency Standard & Poor's said it was keeping Niagara Mohawk's debt under review for a possible upgrade.

S&P said it was reviewing the agreement and would meet with Niagara management in the immediate future, prior to determining whether it would raise the company's corporate credit, senior secured, senior unsecured or preferred stock ratings.
S&P is considering a move higher within the "distinctly speculative" category, which spans from B-minus to BB-plus.
S&P currently rates Niagara Mohawk's senior secured debt at BB-minus, its senior unsecured debt at single-B and the firm's preferred stock at B-minus.
Niagara Mohawk is an upstate New York electric and gas utility.
